newsitem.title: USA: Head of FBI in N.Y. angry at air safety board.
newsitem.headline: Head of FBI in N.Y. angry at air safety board.

text.p: The FBI is still investigating whether a bomb or missile downed TWA flight 800 even though transportation officials lean toward mechanical failure as the cause of the crash, a FBI spokesman said on Saturday.

"The FBI position is that it is not helpful to the investigation for either identified or unidenfied investigators to be speculating as to the cause of the crash," the head of the agency's New York City office, James Kallstrom, said through his spokesman.

"The fact of the matter is that all three theories -- a bomb, a missile or mechanical failure -- continue to be under active investigation," said Joseph Valiquette, a spokesman for the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

On Friday, the National Transpiration Safety Board said evidence from the wreckage of the airliner was "consistent" with a fuel tank explosion, and the agency proposed new steps to prevent fuel from reaching flash point.
The board said reconstruction of the plane showed the Boeing 747's center wing's partially full fuel tank to be deformed "consistent with an explosion originating within the tank."
The Paris-bound TWA flight explosed on July 17 shortly after takeoff from New York's Kennedy Airport and plunged into the Atlantic Ocean, killing all 230 people on board.
According to news report, investigators believe a spark from an unknown source, possibly static electricity, could have ignited the vapors in the fuel tank.
Kallstrom said that he is not aware of any evidence that static electricity was the ignition source.
